unified_issues.description: fastSine() backs its sine lookup with a function-local static SineTable whose juce::dsp::LookupTableTransform::initialise() allocates a 1024-point table. All call sites (DrumVoiceEngine.h:106,157,217) are reached only from processBlock, so on the very first block that renders a tonal voice the static is lazily constructed on the audio thread — a one-time heap allocation plus a one-time thread-safe-static (__cxa_guard) lock acquisition. Not a per-block hazard, but it is an allocation/lock reachable from the audio thread on the first call.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Warm up the lookup table off the audio thread by calling fastSine once during prepareToPlay (or constructing the table eagerly as a namespace-scope object) so the static is fully initialized before the first processBlock, eliminating the first-block allocation and guard lock.

unified_issues.description: sequencerMidi.ensureSize(4096) preallocates the merged MIDI buffer, but the code permits up to kMaxFiringColumns (128) firing columns per block x 6 voices = ~768 emitted note-ons (plus carry-over and host MIDI). At ~9-12 bytes per MidiBuffer event that worst case can exceed 4096 bytes, in which case MidiBuffer::addEvent would reallocate on the audio thread. The 128-column count is a generous safety cap that is unreachable at realistic block sizes/tempos (a normal block spans 1-3 sixteenths), so this is theoretical, but the reserve is not provably sufficient for the bound the code itself allows.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Size sequencerMidi.ensureSize for the actual worst-case event count (kMaxFiringColumns * kNumVoices * bytesPerEvent plus host headroom), or clamp the number of emitted events per block to a value the reserve covers, so addEvent can never reallocate.

unified_issues.description: processBlock has no explicit early return for an empty buffer (e.g. if (buffer.getNumSamples() == 0) return;). The current code is provably safe with numSamples==0 (clear, clock window, render loop, and gain/scrub loops all no-op), but the defensive zero-length guard is a standard buffer-handling pattern and its absence is the only checklist gap here.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Add an explicit early-out at the top of processBlock when getNumSamples()==0 to make the empty-buffer contract explicit and guard future edits that might assume numSamples>0.

unified_issues.description: Per-voice Level (and Tune/Decay/Tone) are pushed to the voices once per block via voices.setParams and applied as a direct multiply/coefficient with no SmoothedValue. Only the master outputLevel is smoothed. Fast host automation of a per-voice Level could produce a small per-block step (zipper) on a sustaining tail. Acceptable for short percussion one-shots, but it is a smoothing gap relative to the master path.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: If per-voice level automation is expected, wrap each voice's level gain in a juce::SmoothedValue (or ramp it across the block) the way outputGain is handled; otherwise document the per-block application as an accepted percussion-one-shot tradeoff.

unified_issues.description: ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 names a 'Mixer / Master' component ('Custom sum + juce::SmoothedValue<float> on output gain'). The implementation satisfies this functionally -- per-voice level is applied inside each voice, voices ADD into a shared cleared buffer (the 'custom sum'), and the master gain is a SmoothedValue applied in an inline per-sample loop -- but there is no discrete Mixer struct/class, so the named component has no one-to-one source mapping. This is acceptable peripheral drift, not a missing component.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: Optional only: extract the inline master-gain loop (PluginProcessor.cpp:350-360) into a small OSimpleBeatmaker::Mixer struct for one-to-one traceability to ARCHITECTURE section 5; the 'custom sum + SmoothedValue' contract is already met so no change is required to pass the gate.

unified_issues.description: Host-MIDI note-ons push a VizEvent (source=1) for any GM-mapped note unconditionally, whereas the audio path gates muted/non-soloed voices in UnifiedTriggerRouter::handleTrigger. For a voice played via host MIDI while muted (or while another voice is soloed), the live MIDI readout would show an event with no corresponding audio. QUAL-02 (the sequencer applied-Delta-t truth, which the timing lane depends on) is unaffected because the sequencer path gates before emit (PluginProcessor.cpp:307); this only concerns the host-MIDI live readout. May be intentional, since ARCHITECTURE section 6 frames it as a 'live MIDI note-on readout' of incoming MIDI.
unified_issues.fixSuggestion: If the readout should mirror audio under mute/solo, gate the host-MIDI viz push with router.isVoiceAudible(voice) in PluginProcessor.cpp:332; otherwise document in VizAnalyzer.h that the host-MIDI readout intentionally shows incoming MIDI pre-mute. Resolve as a Stage-3 UI decision.
